title: Baire category theorem for a complete linearly topologized abelian group with a countable fundamental system
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the Baire category theorem in the form this chapter needs: for a linearly topologized complete abelian group with a countable fundamental system of neighbourhoods of zero, a countable intersection of open dense subsets is dense (statement lines 9037-9042). The proof is a full 31-line construction (proof lines 9045-9075): after replacing the U_n by their finite intersections it builds, for a prescribed point x and a prescribed neighbourhood M_k of zero, a sequence y_i with y_i in U_i and y_i - y_{i-1} in M_{k_{i-1}}, where the indices k_i are chosen increasing so that y_i + M_{k_i} sits inside U_i, then uses completeness to produce the limit y and shows x - y is in M_k and y is in every U_i. The two places where the topology is really consumed are the choice of each k_i, which needs openness of U_i, and the passage to the limit, which needs completeness of M; the proof closes with the telescoping identity for y - y_i, so no step is left as routine.
